lines.trans: Hey boss, business sure looks like it's booming for you!

words.gram: Auxiliary na-adjective expressing appearance or likeness.

lines.trans: Sporting a fancy jacket that doesn't even suit you!
It's the era we're in — new video shops keep multiplying without my lifting a finger.
Look at you smoking classy cigarettes now — let me bum one.
Quit ribbing me over every little detail.
More importantly, how's your next release coming? Still feuding with the regulation commission?
Yeah, we're still locked horns with them.
Remember, I'm a genuine fan of Sapphire's work.
As long as you clear the commission, I'll stock as many copies in my stores as you want.
I'm holding you to that promise right now!
Wait — did you finish a brand-new video already?!
Barkeeper — one bottle of beer and two glasses!
Hey boss, business sure looks like it's booming for you!

meanings.note: In もういい, means 'already enough' or 'ready now'.
Auxiliary na-adjective expressing resemblance or conjecture.

examples.trans: It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.text: 彼は忙しいみたいですね。

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: 似合わないジャケットなんか着ちゃって。
examples.trans: Sporting a fancy jacket that doesn't even suit you!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Colloquial particle, often used to downplay or dismiss.

examples.text: テレビなんか見ていないで勉強しろ。
コーヒーなんかどうですか。
examples.trans: How about some coffee or something?

meanings.note: Noun.

examples.text: 時代が変わりましたね。

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Expresses frustration, regret, or surprise that reality contradicts what was expected; often trails off at the end of a spoken complaint.

examples.text: 約束したのに来なかった。
examples.trans: Even though they promised, they did not come.

examples.text: せっかくの休みなのに。
examples.trans: Even though it is a hard-earned day off.

meanings.note: Core noun for any retail shop or café; often takes polite お to become お店.

examples.trans: There is a shop in front of the station.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Intransitive ichidan verb meaning something increases in number or amount.

examples.text: 最近お客さんが増えました。
仕事が増えて忙しくなりました。
examples.trans: Work increased and I got busy.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Number 一 + counter 本 (with sound change to いっぽん).

examples.text: ペンを一本貸してください。

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

そんな.gloss: such; that kind of; that much

meanings.note: Before たくさん, means 'that huge an amount'.

examples.text: そんな話は知りません。
examples.trans: I do not know such a story.

examples.text: そんな高いものは買えません。
examples.trans: I cannot buy something that expensive.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Used with の to modify the following noun (次のお二人様, 次の駅).

examples.trans: I get off at the next station.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Adverb.

examples.text: まだ終わっていません。
笛の音で想像する分、効果的だよ。規制委員会の規定にもクリアしてる。
examples.trans: Because the whistle sparks the imagination, the thick mosaic actually works—and clears every rule!

examples.text: そんなことより、次の作品どうなってんだ？まだ規制委員会とモメてんのか？
examples.trans: More importantly, how's your next release coming? Still feuding with the regulation commission?

examples.text: そんなバカな…そもそも我々は規制委員会に加盟していない！
examples.trans: That's absurd — we aren't even members of your regulation commission in the first place!

examples.text: そんなことより、次の作品どうなってんだ？まだ規制委員会とモメてんのか？
examples.trans: More importantly, how's your next release coming? Still feuding with the regulation commission?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.

examples.text: 仮に女優が見つかったとしても、その委員会が許可しねえと販売できねえってことか。
examples.trans: So even if we somehow found an actress, we can't sell a tape unless that commission approves it?

examples.text: でも、委員会の規制を守らないかぎり作品は出せませんよ。
examples.trans: Even so, unless we abide by the commission's regulations, we won't be able to release the film.

examples.text: 委員会さえクリアすりゃ、今ならいくらでも店に置いてやるぞ。
examples.trans: As long as you clear the commission, I'll stock as many copies in my stores as you want.

examples.text: 過去さえ忘れりゃ簡単にもうけられる仕事だ。贅沢な悩みだろ？
examples.trans: Forget the past and it is easy money. Quite a luxury of a dilemma, right?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Verbal noun; 約束する means 'to promise'.

examples.text: 約束の時間に遅れました。
examples.trans: I was late for the appointment time.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Expresses sudden surprise, shock, or disbelief.

examples.text: えっ、もう帰るんですか。
examples.trans: Huh, are you going home already?

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'glass'.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
